title: Engineering Foundations: 72 sequenced lessons, 10 native workshops and residency bridges
disclaimer: Formative checks are visible in the browser. Progress is self-reported, local and NOT proof of code proficiency.

units.title: Python & program structure
units.overview: An engineer must read unfamiliar code, model invariants, and predict how values move between functions. Python is not merely syntax: students must distinguish mutable from immutable objects, handle untrusted input deliberately, and isolate logic so it can be tested. In the banking service, a request handler calls functions that query records and produce dictionaries. Understanding these boundaries is essential before fixing a ticket.

units.title: HTTP, APIs & network contracts
units.overview: An HTTP API is a public contract across process boundaries. A successful socket connection says little about whether a response is valid or safe. Engineers need to reason about methods, paths, headers, status codes, representations, authorization boundaries, timeouts and retries. The banking residency begins with a /health contract and eventually serves user-specific resources; both require predictable responses and failure semantics.

units.title: SQL & relational data modeling
units.overview: Real applications store data that must survive crashes and concurrent requests. Relational modeling, parameterized queries, constraints, transactions and isolation are foundational to secure backend work. A banking system has correctness invariants: balance must be represented precisely, transfers must not partially apply, and every returned record must be scoped to an authorized caller.

units.title: Testing & quality engineering
units.overview: A useful test is a reproducible claim about behavior. Tests should isolate assumptions, cover expected and failure cases, and survive implementation refactors without encoding private details. Northstar’s banking code has contract and integration suites; an engineer should understand why a test exists, how to reproduce it, and whether a passing suite actually establishes the property claimed.

units.title: Debugging & observability
units.overview: Debugging is disciplined hypothesis testing. A ticket gives symptoms, but the engineer must establish a reproducible scenario, localize the fault, examine runtime evidence, create a minimal fix, and guard against regression. Logging, traces and stack traces are clues, not conclusions. Sensitive information must not be exposed in diagnostic output.

units.title: Computer science & engineering reasoning
units.overview: Computer science fundamentals help engineers predict behavior before deploying code. Choosing data structures affects performance; understanding state and invariants prevents financial correctness bugs; tracing dependencies and failure modes turns complicated software into understandable components. This unit introduces reasoning skills that should carry into later discrete mathematics, algorithms and systems engineering.

units.title: Linux, processes & development environments
units.overview: Process lifecycle, permissions, configuration and safe command execution are core workplace requirements. Learners reproduce faults with actual Python subprocesses and demonstrate resource cleanup.

units.title: Networking, sockets & service operations
units.overview: Understand the packet-to-API stack and its trust boundaries: IP and ports, TCP stream framing, TLS, HTTP and proxies. Real network faults reveal why a green socket is not the same as a correct service.

units.title: Data structures & algorithms
units.overview: Choose and justify collections and complexity using authentic account, job-queue and dependency examples. Practice invariants and performance before using these concepts in banking workflows.

units.title: Software architecture & system design
units.overview: Trace code and data through explicit modules, isolate transport from business policy, and reason about migration, failure modes and reliability before implementing advanced service changes.

lessons.explanation: A function is a contract: it specifies what inputs it accepts, what result it produces, and how invalid inputs behave. Do not hide failure by silently substituting a default; callers may mistake an invalid account for a valid one. lessons.explanation: An HTTP request contains a method, target, headers and optionally a body. The response returns a status, headers and representation. The URL identifies the resource; it is not a guarantee of access. Application code should parse input without assuming clients are honest. Content-Type: application/json

lessons.explanation: GET retrieves a representation without intentionally changing server state. POST usually submits a state-changing operation. objectives: Explain retries, idempotency and failure analysis in the context of a real system
Interpret a worked example and its failure modes
Apply the concept in a runnable Python workshop
lessons.explanation: Networks can fail after a request succeeds but before the response reaches the client. A client that retries an operation may accidentally execute it twice. GET is intended to be safe; a POST transfer is not automatically idempotent. Use a server-enforced idempotency key with a consistent request fingerprint, durable storage and atomic result recording. The client should distinguish timeouts from documented 4xx outcomes.

Content-Type: application/json

{"from":1,"to":2,"cents":500}
lessons.walkthrough: A repeated request with the same key and same content must not repeat the debit. A reused key with different content must not silently adopt the first result.

lessons.explanation: One transfer modifies at least two balances; the updates must succeed together or not at all. An index accelerates predicates at the cost of write/storage overhead; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reveals actual access paths.

lessons.explanation: A test suite is evidence, not proof that software is correct. A regression test should reproduce a real failure before you fix it and pass afterward. CI should fail on regressions and provide reproducible diagnostic output.
